formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Once the signature is submitted, the signer's (owner's) DAI allowance for `spender` is set to `value`. This replaces any earlier allowance and does not add to it.
If `value` equals type(uint256).max, transferFrom and burn never reduce the allowance, so the spender can move all of the signer's DAI with no limit.
The spender can move the signer's DAI with transferFrom, and can also burn it with burn(from, value), up to the allowance.
The signature can only be submitted up to `deadline`. After it is used, the allowance has no expiry.
The signer's permit nonce goes up by one when the signature is used.
formats.shown: The screen reads "Authorize spending of tokens" and shows the spender as a raw address, the max spending amount in DAI ("Unlimited" at 2^255 or above), the deadline as "Valid until" and the owner. The nonce is hidden.

findings.title: Permit has no test case, so no test covers the rendering of the amount, the Unlimited threshold or the deadline.
findings.evidence: FORMATS.md: "cases: 0 (no tx)" for Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline). dai.sol Dai.transferFrom: `if (allowed != type(uint256).max)` treats the max value as unlimited.
findings.fix: Add a test with an EIP-712 Permit message on chain 42161 that uses this DAI verifyingContract. Include one case with value = type(uint256).max to show "Unlimited", and one with a finite amount.

findings.title: Permit intent does not say the allowance replaces the old one or that the spender can also burn the DAI.
findings.evidence: dai.sol Dai.permit: `allowance[owner][spender] = value;` and Dai.burn spends `allowance[from][msg.sender]`. Descriptor intent: "Authorize spending of tokens".
findings.fix: Optionally change the intent to "Set DAI allowance for spender".
